text: Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
So Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, after Moses had sent her home,

versions.text: So Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, after he had sent her home,
versions.explanation: In the current wording, "he" most naturally attaches to Jethro, the subject of the sentence, whereas the Hebrew ("after her sending away") means Moses had sent her back. Naming Moses removes the ambiguity for a listener and matches the naming of Moses in the next verse.

text: along with her two sons. One was named Gershom, for Moses had said, "I have been a stranger in a foreign land,"
and the other Eliezer, for he said, "The God of my father was my help; he rescued me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with Moses' sons and his wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God.
He sent word to Moses: "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife with her two sons."
Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him. They greeted each other warmly and then went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, and about all the hardships they had met along the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
Jethro rejoiced over all the good the LORD had done for Israel in rescuing them from the hand of the Egyptians.
And Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who delivered the people from under Egypt's hand.

Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods, for he acted against those who dealt so arrogantly with them." [Footnote: The end of this verse is difficult in Hebrew; it reads literally "for in the matter in which they acted arrogantly against them."]

versions.text: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods, for he acted against those who dealt so arrogantly with them."
versions.explanation: The final clause is notoriously obscure in Hebrew and the rendering supplies a subject ("he acted") not present in the text; a brief footnote would alert the reader that the interpretation is uncertain.

text: Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.
The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.

When Moses' father-in-law saw everything he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?"
Moses answered his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
Whenever they have a dispute, it comes to me, and I decide between one person and another, and I make known God's statutes and his laws."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good.
You will wear yourself out, and these people with you, for the task is too heavy for you. You cannot do it alone.
Now listen to me, and let me give you advice, and may God be with you. You represent the people before God and bring their cases to him.
Teach them the statutes and the laws, and show them the way they are to walk and what they are to do.
And you are to look out from all the people for capable men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate a bribe, and appoint them over the people as officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

versions.text: But choose from all the people capable men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate a bribe, and appoint them over the people as officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew "וְאַתָּה תֶחֱזֶה" continues Jethro's instruction ("and you shall look for/select") rather than contrasting with it; "But" introduces an adversative sense not present in the text and breaks the flow from verse 20.

text: Let them judge the people at all times. Every major case they shall bring to you, but every minor case they shall decide themselves. So lighten your load and let them carry it with you.
If you do this, and God so commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people will go home in peace."
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
He chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people: officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people at all times. The difficult cases they brought to Moses, but every minor case they decided themselves.
Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and he returned to his own land.
